title: Hardik Pandya to Return via Domestic Cricket, Shubman Gill Says
excerpt: The injured all-rounder, rehabilitating in Bengaluru since June after quad and shin injuries, must prove his fitness in domestic cricket before an India comeback, his captain confirmed.
body:
• India captain Shubman Gill said Hardik Pandya will play domestic cricket before returning to the national side, after a niggle again delayed the all-rounder's comeback.
  • Pandya has been rehabilitating at the BCCI Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru since June, after a quadriceps strain was followed by a shin injury, RevSportz reported.
  • He has not played for India since the T20 World Cup final on March 8 this year, and has not featured in an ODI since the Champions Trophy final on March 9, 2025.
  • India begin a five-match ODI series against New Zealand at Eden Park, Auckland on November 4 without Pandya.

Hardik Pandya's return to the India team will come through domestic cricket, captain Shubman Gill said ahead of the ODI series opener against New Zealand, after another injury setback delayed the all-rounder's comeback. Pandya was named in the India A squad for the one-day series against Australia A in Puducherry in October, but a niggle shortly before those matches sidelined him again, Gill told reporters in Auckland.

"It's been very unfortunate that he hasn't been able to play since the IPL. And yes, we have had multiple conversations. He was supposed to play the India matches, but just before that he got some niggles again. So hopefully, he will be fit soon and will play some domestic cricket and then hopefully we will see him back in the side soon."

— Shubman Gill, India captain, via RevSportz

A long road back

Pandya, 33, has been doing rehabilitation at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru since June, RevSportz reported. He initially had a quad strain, recovered from that, and then suffered a shin injury. He has not featured in an ODI since the Champions Trophy final on March 9, 2025, and his last appearance in international cricket was the T20 World Cup final on March 8 this year, according to RevSportz. Since then he has missed India's home series against Afghanistan, tours of Ireland and England, and the home ODI series against the West Indies, and he is missing the current tour of New Zealand, according to reporting carried by 7Globe. On October 22, RevSportz reported, quoting a source, that Pandya cannot return until he is 110 per cent fit and should be completely fit in two months — a timeline that makes him touch-and-go for the knockout phase of the Vijay Hazare Trophy starting January 2, 2027.

Why India feel the absence

Gill described a fast-bowling all-rounder who can bowl with the new ball, in the middle overs and at the death, alongside his batting, as a quality few players in the world possess, RevSportz reported. In Pandya's absence, the team management has tried to fill the seam-bowling all-rounder role through Nitish Reddy in the 50-over format and a seamer who can bat at No. 8, the report said. Gill also said Pandya's return would settle the No. 7 and No. 8 batting positions: "Whenever Hardik bhai comes back, no 7/8 will also be taken care of," he said, according to 7Globe.

What's next

India begin their five-match ODI series against New Zealand at Eden Park in Auckland on November 4, with further matches in Wellington on November 7 and Hamilton on November 10, followed by two matches in Mount Maunganui on November 13 and 15, according to 7Globe. The series will be played without Pandya and without Jasprit Bumrah, RevSportz reported. Gill said a series win in those circumstances would give the group confidence that any version of the side can beat other teams under any conditions, with the ODI World Cup in view. For Pandya, the next step is match fitness in domestic cricket — and, on the reporting so far, no return date has been set.
